portal_solution:
Before applying this update, make sure all previously released errata
relevant to your system have been applied.

This update is available via the Red Hat Network. Details on how to
use the Red Hat Network to apply this update are available at
https://access.redhat.com/site/articles/11258
portal_description:
Red Hat Identity Management is a centralized authentication, identity management
and authorization solution for both traditional and cloud-based enterprise
environments. It integrates components of the Red Hat Directory Server, MIT
Kerberos, Red Hat Certificate System, NTP, and DNS. It provides web browser and
command-line interfaces. Its administration tools allow an administrator to
quickly install, set up, and administer a group of domain controllers to meet
the authentication and identity management requirements of large-scale Linux and
UNIX deployments.

This update fixes the following bug:

* Identity Management Server (IdM Server) and the underlying Certificate
Authority component (PKI) had different expectations regarding certificates
passed by the "--external_cert_file" option of the ipa-server-install command.
As a consequence, when IdM Server was installed with a PKI being chained to
external Certificate Authority (CA), installation could terminate unexpectedly
with the following error message:

    ipa-server-install --external_cert_file ipa-ca.crt --external_ca_file 
    external-ca.crt
    ...
    [16/22]: restarting certificate server
    [17/22]: requesting RA certificate from CA
    Unexpected error - see /var/log/ipaserver-install.log for details:
    IndexError: list index out of range

The PEM certificate passed in the "--external_ca_file" option has been converted
to PKCS#7 format expected by PKI, and IdM Server installation with CA
certificate signed by external CA now succeeds. (BZ#1130031)

Users of ipa are advised to upgrade to these updated packages, which fix this
bug.
